- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.3) and forecast is still trending up, adjust downward by 3–5% to reflect mean reversion.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 price points in history are trending down, model should not overcorrect upward; cap forecast rise to 1–2% above recent low.  
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (±0.2–0.5) and forecast is volatile, smooth transitions by averaging 2–3 prior forecast values before next step.  
- When true outcome deviates > 3% from forecast in early days (1–7), check if sentiment was high at that time — if so, reduce forecast by 1–2% to account for sentiment-driven overreaction.  
- For long-term (15+ day) forecasts, if sentiment is consistently positive, allow slight upward bias but cap at 1.5% above recent 10-day average to avoid overconfidence.
